turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that the threat was not merely from the Muslims but also from the suffering of his people under Sandip’s oppressive rule, and that he must remove himself from Nikhil’s lands.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his concerns were misplaced, for Sandip’s actions were driven by a higher purpose and a desire to uplift the nation, not to oppress or intimidate anyone.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip’s so-called higher purpose was in fact a facade for personal ambition and manipulation, causing suffering and division among the people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip insisted that his actions were not about personal ambition but a noble quest to awaken the nation from its slumber, and that any perceived oppression was a necessary evil in the grand scheme of progress.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his rhetoric about national awakening was nothing more than a smokescreen for his true intentions, which were clear to Nikhil and the people he represented.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his intentions were pure, driven by a desire to liberate the nation from the shackles of colonial rule and to awaken the masses to the reality of their oppression.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip’s noble quest was nothing but a guise for his true nature, one that sought to manipulate and exploit the vulnerabilities of the people for his own gain.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his intentions were as pure as they were misunderstood, asserting that he sought to liberate the nation from the chains of colonial rule, even if it meant taking actions that others might not comprehend or approve of.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he was well aware of the facade of noble intentions and the reality of Sandip’s true motives, which were transparent to Nikhil and the people he represented.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his actions, though misunderstood and often maligned, were driven by a deep-seated desire to see the nation rise from its colonial slumber, even if it meant taking harsh measures that some found disagreeable.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip’s harsh measures were not only detrimental to the stability and security of the land but also a direct threat to the safety and livelihood of his tenants, many of whom were already suffering.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his actions were a necessary evil, born from a fervent desire to see the nation free and strong, even if it meant taking steps that others found harsh or threatening.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that the facade of liberation was marred by the reality of oppression, and that such actions could only lead to further division and suffering among the people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he understood the concerns but dismissed them as the misgivings of a man trapped in the old ways, blind to the revolutionary spirit needed to break free from colonial shackles.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the path to true liberation lay in unity and justice, not in oppression and division, and that Sandip’s methods were undermining the very fabric of society.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala told Sandip and Nikhil that she understood their perspectives but felt conflicted, as she admired Sandip's revolutionary spirit but also valued Nikhil's wisdom and sense of justice.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he could see the wisdom in Bimala’s conflicted perspective but maintained that the path to real liberation was often paved with tough choices and that his methods, though harsh, were necessary to awaken the nation from its slumber.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala told Sandip and Nikhil that she felt torn between their opposing views, recognizing the righteousness in Nikhil’s call for unity and justice and the urgency in Sandip’s revolutionary fervor.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip’s methods were sowing discord and would only lead to further division, undermining the stability and security that were essential for any true progress.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he understood Nikhil’s concerns but believed that true change often came at a cost, and that the current hardships were merely the birth pangs of a new era.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would flee, Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was just telling Queen Bee about their college club and the contest over the translation of lines from Browning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that he managed to translate the lines into Bengali but doubted it would be a joy forever for the people of Bengal, and recalled old Dakshina's rendering, adding that Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if the warning was about the fever fit of poesy.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up local Mussulmans and that they might attack Sandip any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise flight.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and suggested that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he did not offer advice and wished Sandip would refrain from giving him advice, and that he must ask Sandip to leave his territory due to the worrying and oppression of his tenantry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if the threat was for fear of the Mussulmans or if there was another fear.
